bug_description.original: Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=4908620733349888 Project: cups Fuzzing Engine: libFuzzer Fuzz Target: FuzzCUPS Job Type: libfuzzer_asan_cups Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free READ {*} Crash State: copy_stack _cupsRasterExecPS FuzzCUPS.c Sanitizer: address (ASAN)
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 27-byte ASCII witness `1/// 1// 1/ 8 copy/ 18 copy` is duplicated by `FuzzCUPS` and interpreted by `_cupsRasterExecPS()` as CUPS' PostScript mini-language. `scan_ps()` materializes the prefix `1/// 1// 1/` as nine initial stack objects, the first `8 copy` duplicates eight of them to raise `st->num_objs` from 9 to 17 without exhausting the initial 32-slot stack buffer, the following bare `/` makes the live depth 18, and the final `18 copy` asks `copy_stack()` to duplicate the entire live stack. Vulnerable `copy_stack()` passes `st->objs + n` directly back into `push_stack()`. On the 15th push of that final copy, `push_stack()` sees `st->num_objs >= st->alloc_objs`, grows `st->objs` with `realloc()`, and frees the old 2304-byte array while its `obj` parameter still aliases `st->objs[14]` inside that freed region. The subsequent `memcpy(temp, obj, sizeof(_cups_ps_obj_t))` reads 72 bytes from freed heap memory, matching the saved AddressSanitizer stack `push_stack -> copy_stack -> _cupsRasterExecPS`. The fixing commit resolves this exact lifetime bug by copying `st->objs[n]` into a local `_cups_ps_obj_t temp` before calling `push_stack()`.

source.description: First project-code statement on the crashing path that materializes attacker-controlled PostScript tokens into the heap-backed interpreter stack. Repeated `scan_ps()` calls over the witness prefix `1/// 1// 1/` push three numbers and six empty-name objects into `st->objs`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 27-byte ASCII string `1/// 1// 1/ 8 copy/ 18 copy`. Its prefix `1/// 1// 1/` tokenizes as `NUMBER(1)`, `NAME("")`, `NAME("")`, `NAME("")`, `NUMBER(1)`, `NAME("")`, `NAME("")`, `NUMBER(1)`, `NAME("")` because each bare `/` becomes an empty PostScript name token in `scan_ps()`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. After `realloc()` frees the old 32-object stack buffer, this `memcpy` reads one 72-byte `_cups_ps_obj_t` through the stale `obj` pointer that still aliases the freed `st->objs[14]` element.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `heap-use-after-free READ of size 72` at `cups/raster-interpret.c:955:3`, with the freeing call in `push_stack` line 944 during the same `copy_stack` loop.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `copy_stack()` passes a pointer to an element inside the mutable `st->objs` array back into `push_stack()`. If `push_stack()` must grow that array, its internal `realloc()` can free `st->objs` before the aliased element is copied. The fix breaks this alias by copying `st->objs[n]` into a local temporary first.
root_cause.note: In the crashing second `18 copy`, the 15th loop iteration reaches this call with `n == 14` while the live count is already 32, so the incoming `obj` points at the old `st->objs[14]` element exactly when `push_stack()` enters its growth path.

tainted_value_origin.description: The suffix digits `18` in the staged witness are parsed into the numeric copy count used by the final `copy` operator. Because this parsed count equals the current live stack depth after the preceding tokens, `_cupsRasterExecPS()` later calls `copy_stack(st, 18)` and forces the realloc/use-after-free path.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: In the exact witness bytes, the ASCII substring `18` immediately before the last `copy` token becomes this number.

parser_admitted.description: After the size guard and NUL-termination copy, the harness passes the entire staged witness string unchanged into `_cupsRasterExecPS()`. No project-side parser rewrites the bytes before the vulnerable PostScript interpreter consumes them.

fine_trace.note: Allocation. `_cupsRasterExecPS()` creates a fresh stack with `alloc_objs = 32`. AddressSanitizer's allocation stack shows that the later-freed 2304-byte region was allocated by this `calloc()`, so this is the heap object whose lifetime is later broken.

Source. Repeated `scan_ps()` iterations over the witness prefix `1/// 1// 1/` push three numeric `1` objects and six empty-name objects into the heap array, yielding the exact 9-object base stack consumed by the first `copy` operator.
The token `8` is parsed into the numeric count for the first copy operation and is then pushed onto the live stack by line 1377 before the following operator token is processed.
The following token `copy` is recognized as `CUPS_PS_COPY` and pushed onto the stack, selecting the `_cupsRasterExecPS()` switch arm that consumes the `8` from step 3.
The first `CUPS_PS_COPY` dispatch pops the parsed count `8` and invokes `copy_stack(st, 8)`. After the operator and count are removed, 9 live objects remain on the stack.

For the first copy, `n = 9 - 8 = 1`, so the loop duplicates `st->objs[1]` through `st->objs[8]`. Those eight pushes grow the live depth only from 9 to 17, so the stack stays within the original 32-slot allocation and no `realloc()` happens yet.

After the first copy, the next witness byte is a bare `/`. `scan_ps()` turns it into one more empty-name object and pushes it at index 17, bringing the live stack depth to 18 before the final numeric count is read.
The suffix digits `18` are parsed into the numeric count for the final copy. This attacker-controlled value matches the current live stack depth established by steps 6-7.
The final token `copy` is recognized as the copy operator and pushed onto the stack, arming the second `CUPS_PS_COPY` dispatch.

The second `CUPS_PS_COPY` dispatch pops the parsed count `18` and invokes `copy_stack(st, 18)`. After the operator and count are removed, exactly 18 objects remain on the live stack, so this call duplicates the entire stack.
For the final copy, `n = 18 - 18 = 0`, so the loop will start re-reading `st->objs[0]`, then `st->objs[1]`, and eventually every other live stack element directly from the current heap buffer.

Root cause. `copy_stack()` passes a pointer into `st->objs` back into `push_stack()`. On the 15th push of the final `18 copy`, `n == 14`, so the incoming `obj` aliases `st->objs[14]` inside the original 32-slot buffer exactly when that buffer is already full.

The 15th push of the final copy reaches `push_stack()` with `st->num_objs == 32` and `st->alloc_objs == 32`, so this growth check becomes true. Execution enters the reallocation block while `obj` from step 12 still aliases the old stack buffer.

Invalidation. The true branch from step 13 grows the stack to 64 objects with `realloc()`, and ASan reports that this call frees the original 2304-byte region `[0x61d000000080,0x61d000000980)`. The incoming `obj` still points 1008 bytes into that freed region, which corresponds to the old `st->objs[14]` element.

Sink. After step 14's `realloc()` has freed the old `st->objs` buffer, `memcpy()` reads one 72-byte `_cups_ps_obj_t` through the stale `obj` pointer instead of from live memory. The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports the resulting heap-use-after-free read at this line.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix changes `copy_stack()` to copy `st->objs[n]` into a local `_cups_ps_obj_t temp` and then call `push_stack(st, &temp)`, so `push_stack()` no longer receives a pointer into the reallocatable `st->objs` array. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, exact staged vulnerable source from the ARVO workspace container, and patch.diff; Stage 02 did not run fixed-version validation

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable reproduction ran `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_54069 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which executed `/out/FuzzCUPS /tmp/poc` inside the ARVO workspace and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 72` in `push_stack -> copy_stack -> _cupsRasterExecPS`.

format.name: CUPS PostScript mini-interpreter program
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 27-byte ASCII witness `1/// 1// 1/ 8 copy/ 18 copy` (sha256 `093de096c3ee252659f3299eabc84494ce689ae0d436a780853a6028e3e9ac7d`). Its prefix `1/// 1// 1/` must still tokenize as three numeric `1` objects and six empty-name objects, the subsequence `8 copy` must still raise the live stack from 9 to 17 objects without reallocating, the following bare `/` must still raise the live depth to 18, and the final `18 copy` must still request duplication of all 18 live objects so the 15th push runs with `st->num_objs == st->alloc_objs == 32`. The staged evidence does not justify a broader contract than witnesses preserving that exact tokenization and stack-depth sequence.
